proposed.sourceName: Darul Iftaa, Jaamia Madinatul Uloom Trinidad — 'Is Shellac Halaal?' (Mufti Arshad Ali)
proposed.paraphrase: Rules that shellac (E904), the lac-insect resin used as a glaze in confectionery, bakery and pharmaceutical products, is halal (referencing SANHA).

proposed.sourceName: Darul Ifta Birmingham — 'Confused As to Whether or Not Shellac Is Permissible' (checked by Mufti Mohammed Tosir Miah)
proposed.paraphrase: Rules shellac (E904) impermissible (haram) to consume because it is insect-produced content and insects fall under the 'Hawwam' category that is unlawful to eat — hence confectionery containing shellac is not lawful.

researcherNote: E904 seeded lenient grade 3 (contested). Sharp real split between tier-1 darul-iftaas: Trinidad (citing SANHA) rules shellac halal; Birmingham rules it haram as insect (Hawwam) content. Two independent tier-1, both sides. APPROVED by owner 2026-07-01 (batch pre-approval).
